close_reason: Won't fix in this scope: canonical jmap-mail-server has 0 '# Errors' rustdoc sections across 32 handle_* fns. Adding ~18 '# Errors' sections to calendars-server alone would diverge from canonical, recreating the cookie-cutter regression the rule exists to prevent. Defer to a workspace-wide '# Errors rustdoc sweep' PLAN that touches all 7 extension-server crates uniformly (and ideally the 7 extension-client crates as well per sister JMAP-231o.34 closure rationale).
description:
Every handle_* function in this crate returns Result<(Value, Vec<Invocation>), JmapError>. None of them have a '# Errors' section in their rustdoc enumerating which JmapError types they may produce.

Affected (all 18+ public handle_* fns across calendar.rs, event.rs, event_notification.rs, participant_identity.rs, principal.rs).

The canonical extension-server jmap-mail-server has a similar gap (worth coordinating cross-crate; a doc-comment sweep across all extension-server siblings is the cookie-cutter way to land this). Public Rust libraries documenting error contracts is the modern idiom — clippy::missing_errors_doc is part of pedantic.

Concrete error types each handler can produce (from current code):
- accountNotFound (some, not all — see JMAP-r3pg.4)
- fromAccountNotFound (handle_calendar_event_copy)
- invalidArguments (extract_account_id; non-object payload guard)
- stateMismatch (ifInState handling)
- serverFail (any backend error)
- accountNotFound for /parse and /getAvailability

This isn't a behaviour bug — JmapError is part of the public API and authors of consumer code currently have to read source to discover what to handle.

P4/opinion. JMAP-231o.34 has the same finding for calendars-client. Same fix applies here. Could be batched into a doc-comment sweep across all server crates.
title: Public fallible handlers (handle_*) missing # Errors rustdoc sections
